purpose: Every verifier this corpus has been compared against, with the two fields that decide whether a number may be quoted: independence, and where the evidence for that row lives. An entry is a fact about a recorded run, not a claim about a product.
independence_rule: independent = different maintainer, written from the specification text without reading this repository's reference code. same-maintainer = one of us. tools/check_implementations.py refuses any other word, and refuses 'independent' from this organisation's own repository address.

maintainer.note: A single-operator corpus. The honest label is cheaper than an overclaim someone else disproves later.

implementations.evidence_source: uibc-core docs/SECOND-IMPLEMENTATION.md, tools/cross_impl_check.py --json: strict 36/36, refused 30/36 over 36 packages; enforced by the second-implementation CI job
implementations.coverage_note: S0 is the verifier's own crash line, so a sound package has none to compare.
Exists so the public corpus can be replayed with Node alone, without Python and without reading a second repository. It is not an improvement on verify-js; it is reachability.

Different axis entirely: not 'does it agree on the corpus' but 'how many doctored packages does it accept'. Kept in the same manifest because a reader weighing implementations needs both numbers in one place.

evidence.note: The four counts are recomputed from interop-results.json by tools/check_implementations.py; a stale number fails CI instead of impressing a reader.

known_divergences.what: Whether the evidence root is computed over bytes on disk or over hashes claimed in evidence/index.json. The reference computes it over on-disk bytes, reports S5 as skipped (INCONCLUSIVE) when S4 fails, and S8 as FAIL when the checkpoint over on-disk bytes differs.
known_divergences.disposition: This repository's first cross-run reported PASS for S5/S8 on tampered, deleted and hash-flip packages: arithmetically true, semantically worthless. It was corrected in the same run.
known_divergences.credit: Not a new finding. uibc-core recorded it as bug 3 of four in docs/SECOND-IMPLEMENTATION.md before this repository existed. Re-deriving it from the other side is a check that the documentation is accurate, not a discovery - and it is kept here so that a reader of the public corpus can see the rule rather than have to trust a link.

what_this_manifest_cannot_say: that any implementation is secure or competent
that the corpus is complete - 20 rows is a floor, not a proof
that agreement among same-maintainer implementations is corroboration; it is convergence

how_to_add_an_external_implementation.1: Add one object here with independence='independent', the checks you actually run, and evidence_source pointing at a machine-readable record.
how_to_add_an_external_implementation.2: Either run tools/run_crossimpl.py yourself, or submit results in the same shape as interop-results.json.
how_to_add_an_external_implementation.3: set scored_in_this_run=false and name your own record; the gate does not require your numbers to be ours, only that a checkable record exists.
how_to_add_an_external_implementation.4: A row claiming 'independent' from this organisation's address is refused. The label is checked, not trusted.
